title: What is the smallest angle if two angles fit below sixty?
description: A figure has sixty degrees as an angle of symmetry, with exactly two angles of symmetry smaller than it. The angles are the smallest angle taken one time, two times and three times, so sixty is the third. The answer is checked by listing the angles and dividing the full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: the angles of symmetry are one, two, three times the smallest angle in order, so the third one being sixty gives the smallest angle. Watch for students who call sixty the smallest angle.

source: Figure it Out Q5 (section 9.2, second block)
video_script.why: The child finds the smallest angle of symmetry from the position of a known angle in the list of angles.
video_script.substitution: a figure turned about its dot, with its angles of symmetry placed in order on a number line of degrees
video_script.anchor: a figure with a dot at its centre, and its angles of symmetry placed in order on a line
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest angle of symmetry is twenty degrees
maths_rules: the angles of symmetry are 1 x, 2 x, 3 x, ... the smallest angle
exactly two angles are less than 60°: the smallest angle and 2 x the smallest angle
so 60° is the next one, 3 x the smallest angle
check: 20°, 40° are below 60°, 3 x 20 = 60, and 360 ÷ 20 = 18 is a whole number
video_script.design: The angles of symmetry placed in order on a line, the first two below sixty and sixty as the third. Dividing sixty by three gives the smallest angle, and the list is read back to check.

<bookmark mark='div'/>Step three, divide sixty by three.

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step four, check by listing the angles.
They are twenty, forty and sixty degrees, and exactly two are below sixty.
<bookmark mark='full'/>Three hundred sixty divided by twenty is eighteen, a whole number, so twenty fits into the full turn.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The smallest angle of symmetry is twenty degrees.
